newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's says downward trend in rates continues.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's says downward trend in rates continues.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Friday that there were no signs of reversal of the downward pressure on rates in the insurance market.
The slide in rates is expected to reduce profits in the 1996 underwriting year to around 600 million stg, down from just over one billion stg in 1994.
Many underwriters expect the tough market conditions to continue for at least another year, according to Lloyd's chairman Sir David Rowland.
Marine rates peaked in 1994 and began to fall during 1995 as worldwide capacity increased. These reductions continued in 1996, particularly in hull and energy.
Despite this marine syndicates expect healthy profits for both 1995 and 1996 thanks to selective underwriting and favourable loss experience, said Lloyd's.
Non-marine also suffered from a downturn in rates in 1995 and 1996 but again catastrophe losses have been limited.

In contrast, a high number of aviation catastrophes in 1994 led to a rise in rates in 1995 before peaking in the final quarter of the year. Losses were favourable in 1995 leading to a decline in rates in 1996.
Lloyd's said motor syndicates were projecting a small loss in 1995 after rates continued to fall in 1995 and 1996 as competition intensified.
There are, however, signs that rates have started to move upwards during 1997 and this is expected to lead to a return to profitability.
